types.name: MachineKitRobotCompiler
types.doc: MachineKit mechanical-design to RobotKit execution-model bridge.

fields.name: compileGantry
fields.doc:
Compile the authored gantry, including its drives, through the app's bridge.
Logical ceilings restrict a job; they do not replace physical drive ratings.

fields.name: compileLinearAxis
fields.doc:
Compiles one MachineKit LinearAxis and its logical axis mapping. The
returned blueprint exposes the RobotModel used to create the runtime, so
design, simulation, and deployment all share one compiled description.

fields.name: compileLinearAxisModel
fields.doc: Compiles the same part-level assembly used by the complete motion blueprint.

types.name: ManipulatorKinematics
types.doc:
KinematicsSolver adapter over RobotKit's deterministic DLS manipulator.

A redundant arm (`Manipulator.redundant`, e.g. 7-axis) is handled through
its swivel angle: `solvePose` keeps the seed's swivel as a preference, so
the elbow does not drift with each solve; `sampleCandidates` sweeps the
swivel around the circle on each IK branch it finds; and `solvePath`
chooses the swivel (or a cell's external-axis values) along a whole path
with `RedundancyResolver`.

fields.name: manipulator
fields.doc: The group solved: an arm (`Manipulator`), or an arm with external axes and a work frame.

fields.name: preferredPosture
fields.doc:
A posture the solves draw the arm towards (`q` order): with external
axes, the arm stays comfortable and they bring the work to it.

fields.name: preferredOrientation
fields.doc: Soft tool orientation preference for reduced tasks; hard rows always win.

fields.name: preferTargetOrientation
fields.doc: Prefer each authored orientation softly while preserving the hard task freedom.

fields.name: lastFailure
fields.doc: Residuals from the last failed solve, for planner diagnostics.

fields.name: fork
fields.doc: The same kinematics with its own posture preference; the group is shared, as it is safe to.

fields.name: solvePath
fields.doc:
The path: a redundant arm (7-axis) chooses its swivel along it, a group
with external axes their values, both through `RedundancyResolver`; a
plain arm follows point by point, each sample seeded by the last.

fields.name: solvePathWithRates
fields.doc: The path and, for a redundant group, the exact rate of its redundancy along it (see `RedundancyResolver`).

fields.name: redundancy
fields.doc: How the group's redundancy is named, if it has any: its swivel, else its external axes.

types.name: ManipulatorMotion
types.doc:
Runs manipulator programs and evaluates host-side barriers. A program is
planned as it runs, on a worker thread about `LOOKAHEAD_SECONDS` of motion
ahead of the machine, so neither starting a long program nor running it
waits for planning; only if execution catches up with planning does an
update wait for the next plan.

fields.name: checks
fields.doc: What the plan checks found in the plans this motion has started, if its compiler runs one.

fields.name: slip
fields.doc:
Carries out the stepper slip the plan checks predict, when a simulation sets one. It is fed each plan
as it starts and its elapsed time while it runs.

fields.name: LOOKAHEAD_SECONDS
fields.doc: Seconds of planned motion kept ahead of the machine.

fields.name: speedOverride
fields.doc: Speed of every path, as a fraction of its programmed speed.

fields.name: planningMetrics
fields.doc: Cumulative compilation work across programs; excludes worker lookahead waits.

fields.name: commandedPositions
fields.doc:
The joint positions the last program commanded at its end, which the next program is planned
from; null before any program has finished and after a failure, when the next one starts from
where the robot is.

fields.name: compilationPlanId
fields.doc: First unused ID for a compilation prepared while this motion is idle.

fields.name: run
fields.doc:
Starts `program`. By default it waits for the first plan, so a program that cannot start fails here (`failure`)
before the session begins. With `waitForFirstPlan` false it returns at once and the first plan is made on the
planner thread while the caller keeps its frame: `running` is true meanwhile, and `update` begins the program (or
fails it) when that plan is ready. A deterministic stepper, whose results must not depend on how long planning
takes, waits; an interactive one does not.

fields.name: runCompiled
fields.doc:
Submit checked plans once; ownership passes to this motion after validation.
Their clock and process events are retained without another compiler pass.

fields.name: setSpeedOverride
fields.doc:
Sets the speed override, between 5% and 200% of the programmed speed. A
running program takes it from the motion it has not planned yet, about
`LOOKAHEAD_SECONDS` ahead, within the joint limits and without stopping.

fields.name: stop
fields.doc: Discard the current program with a controlled stop; update confirms rest without creating or clearing a fault.

fields.name: shutdownPlanning
fields.doc:
Cancels this motion's planning and waits before its native planning resources are destroyed.
Other motions and their workers are unaffected. Returns the workers still running at timeout.

types.name: ManipulatorPlannerSpace
types.doc: Maps the active manipulator coordinates into the complete robot's collision-planner state.

fields.name: new
fields.doc: Preserve measured process coordinates outside the arm while varying only the arm DOFs.

types.name: ManipulatorProgress
types.doc: Position in the authored program and current path.

types.name: ManipulatorServo
types.doc:
Bounded differential IK for live servoing (jogging, teleoperation): each
tick turns a requested tool twist (at the TCP, in the group's reference
frame) into joint velocities for the next period `dt`. It is
kinematicskit's `DifferentialIk` on the group's tool `FrameVelocityTask`,
natively on ProxQP:

minimize ½‖J·Δ − twist·dt‖² + ½λ²‖Δ‖²   subject to `StepLimits`

with the group's position limits, its velocity limits (`velocityLimits`
overrides them) and, given `previousVelocity`, its acceleration limits
(`accelerationLimits` overrides them), so the step also never approaches a
stop faster than it can brake. `limitGain` and `ramped` are StepLimits'
(a ramped step is a streamed plan chunk). If the QP does not solve, the
damped step clamped into the same bounds is used, and the answer says so.

With `avoidance` set, each tick asks it for the pairs near the arm at `q`
(bodies of the group's model; another robot or the environment is -1) and
adds their velocity-damper rows (`kinematicskit.AvoidanceRows`, closing at
most `avoidanceSpeed`): the servo stops short of obstacles and slides
along them instead of finding out afterwards (COLLISION.md CL5).

Keep one per arm and reuse it: the QP warm-starts from the previous tick.

types.name: MergeErrorBudget
types.doc:
Joint-position allowances; the shared native merger derives derivative bounds for each actual candidate duration.
With e(0)=e(T)=0, |e'|<=2*epsilon/T or |e''|<=8*epsilon/T^2 each implies |e|<=epsilon
for a continuously differentiable error (piecewise bounded second derivative suffices).
The native merger also checks position error directly, including numerical roundoff.

types.name: MotionAxisCouplings
types.doc: Expand independent task axes through the compiled physical coupling graph.

fields.name: derived
fields.doc:
The joints that follow more than one axis and so belong to none, as one projection (each after the joints it follows,
the axes' joints first). `axes` are the expanded axes. A joint that follows joints no axis drives (an extruder's gear
train) stays where it is and is not in it, unless it mixes those with driven joints, which needs coordinated planning.
A cycle among the couplings is an error.

types.name: MotionFilterSettings
types.doc: The settings of the transforms, from the compiler.

types.name: MotionProgramSkill
types.doc: Runs a planned arm program through the same lifecycle as the other robot skills.

types.name: MotionRequest
types.doc: Inputs to execute after a controlled stop, captured at command time.

types.name: MotionRequestCapture
types.doc: Copies caller-owned command inputs before a stop can defer execution.

types.name: MotionSession
types.doc:
Motion lifecycle. The runtime owns physical rest; only update() may complete
a hold or stop after a snapshot confirms rest.

State       Event                   Result
Idle        begin/hold              Running/Held
Running     hold                    Holding
Holding     rest                    Held
Holding     resume                  Holding (resume pending)
Held        resume                  Running
Running     replace/abort          Stopping(Replan/Discard)
Stopping    hold/resume             Stopping (no runtime command)
Stopping    rest                    Idle, then pending requests may begin
Any         runtime fault/rejection Faulted
Faulted     reset                   Idle, after runtime safety reset
The same transitions govern axis motion and manipulator programs. A program
waiting for a controlled stop is owned by its caller, not by this session.

fields.name: rest
fields.doc: Called only by MotionSystem.update after runtime rest is observed.

types.name: MotionSystem
types.doc:
Semantic machine-axis view over an ordinary RobotKit robot.

The view owns planning and buffered-execution state, while the Robot still
owns snapshots, transport, safety, and lifecycle. Immediate and queued
motions use the same RobotCommand boundary.

Every change of speed stays within the joints' acceleration limits: a hold
slows along the path, a resume speeds back up along it, and a new immediate
move while moving first brings the machine to rest along its current path,
then plans from where it stopped.

fields.name: planCheck
fields.doc: Drive-check settings shared by immediate, queued, path and replacement motion.

fields.name: lastPathValidationReport
fields.doc: Joint and sampled Cartesian checks for the last planned path.

fields.name: isMoving
fields.doc: True while a trajectory is active, held, or waiting to start after a stop.

fields.name: reset
fields.doc: A fault is latched until the application explicitly resets runtime safety.

fields.name: queueDepth
fields.doc: Number of active and waiting trajectories currently owned by the system.

fields.name: queuedDurationSeconds
fields.doc: Remaining duration across the active trajectory and all queued trajectories.

fields.name: progress
fields.doc: Completion fraction of the currently buffered motion, in the range [0, 1].

fields.name: moveAxes
fields.doc:
Plans a coordinated move while leaving unspecified axes at their current
positions, replacing any buffered motion. While the machine is moving it
first stops along its current path; the move is then planned from where
it came to rest and null is returned, as the plan does not exist yet.

fields.name: queueAxes
fields.doc: Adds a coordinated axis move behind all motion already in the buffer.

fields.name: queueTrajectory
fields.doc: Adds an already planned joint trajectory to the execution buffer.

fields.name: moveLinear
fields.doc:
Plans a straight Cartesian move for a direct XYZ gantry. Like moveAxes,
it first stops along the current path when the machine is moving.

fields.name: queueLinear
fields.doc: Adds a straight Cartesian move behind all motion already in the buffer.

fields.name: movePath
fields.doc:
Plans a connected Cartesian polyline for a direct XYZ machine. The path
must start where the machine is, so it cannot replace motion in progress:
hold and wait for rest first.

fields.name: queuePath
fields.doc: Adds a connected Cartesian polyline behind motion already in the buffer.

fields.name: hold
fields.doc: Holds buffered motion and slows to rest along the path without discarding it.

fields.name: resume
fields.doc:
Resumes a held buffer from where it stopped, speeding back up along the
path. If the hold is still slowing down, it resumes once at rest.

fields.name: abort
fields.doc:
Aborts buffered motion. A normal abort slows to rest along the current
path before discarding it; an emergency stop acts immediately.

fields.name: configureRuntimeHoming
fields.doc: Bind the runtime owner and its encoder/slip reset before sensor homing.

fields.name: home
fields.doc: Sensor homing when authored switches exist; coordinate move for unswitched robots.

fields.name: jog
fields.doc:
Plans a bounded timed jog in one logical axis. The endpoint is clamped to
the authored axis limits, while all physical joints in a coordinated axis
group receive the same logical displacement and scaled velocity.

fields.name: update
fields.doc:
Advances the local deterministic clock and submits one complete position
batch. Pass no duration to use the compiled fixed timestep.

types.name: MotionSystemBlueprint
types.doc: Compiled RobotKit model plus the semantic logical-axis view.

fields.name: replacementMarginOwnerPeriods
fields.doc: Smooth replacement lead in owner periods; defaults to two.

fields.name: homingLatencySeconds
fields.doc: Optional measured upper bound for homing command/observation response, in seconds.

fields.name: homingCaptureSpeedLimits
fields.doc:
Optional commissioned final capture speed caps by logical axis, in SI units/s.
Edge capture removes sampling error, but not load-dependent drive deflection.

fields.name: replacementOwnerPeriodSeconds
fields.doc: Owner period used for replacement lead; defaults to fixedTimestepSeconds.

fields.name: ownerPeriodSeconds
fields.doc: The robot owner's control period, seconds: the runtime's, or the fixed timestep where the runtime leaves it to that.

types.name: MotorSpaceConstraints
types.doc: Linear velocity limits in motor coordinates, including shared CoreXY drives.

fields.name: efforts
fields.doc: Each row's effort limit (N m at its motor), or null where the row is not a motor's.

fields.name: of
fields.doc: A planned subset of independent axes; shared followers are derived from their coupling terms.

fields.name: inscribedSpeed
fields.doc:
The speed the planned joints can move at in every direction at once: the radius of the largest ball inside the rows'
bounds, `min(rate / |row|)`. On a CoreXY that is the 45 degree move that turns one motor at its full rate; a firmware
that has one speed for all directions (Klipper's `max_velocity`) can promise no more. `infinity` when no row binds.

fields.name: inscribedAcceleration
fields.doc:
The acceleration the planned axes (`masses`, kg each) can have in every direction at once, the worst direction: a
firmware with one acceleration for all directions (Klipper's `max_accel`) can promise no more. An axis force F
reaches the motors as the torques that do the same work, `tau = (R R^T)^-1 R F` for the rows `R` that have an effort
limit (the least-torque solution; the motors' own `tau = R^-T F` on a CoreXY), so along the unit direction `d` motor
`m` carries `a * |sum_a W[m][a] mass[a] d[a]|` and the direction that loads it most is along `W[m] * mass`:
`min over motors of effort / |W[m] * mass|`. Drag and steady loads are not counted (the axes' own limits are the ones
that carry them). `infinity` when no row has an effort limit.

fields.name: move
fields.doc: A straight joint move with one jerk-limited progress profile, so all motor sums remain bounded.

fields.name: time
fields.doc: Time the axes and linear motor coordinates together; return only the authored joints.

fields.name: prepareStream
fields.doc: Keep shared-drive rows in every streaming solve, selecting physical joints only after timing.

fields.name: validate
fields.doc: Check polynomial extrema after lowering, including between path timing samples.

types.name: NativeCandidateBatch
types.doc: Copy one already-generated native layer and release its temporary storage.

types.name: NativeStreamSegments
types.doc: A plan's segments read in place from native arrays, over the robot's joints.

types.name: NumericBranchIk
types.doc:
Explicit fallback for geometry without a supported analytic family.
Numeric branch IDs identify seeds, not persistent geometric branches.

fields.name: branchesFromNeighbours
fields.doc: Neighbour seeds precede the deterministic fixed set; external coordinates stay held.

types.name: OrientationDifferential
types.doc:
Analytic second-order quaternion composition for a moving orientation
centre, a spline swing vector, and periodic roll. Angular rates are spatial
(expressed in the same reference frame as the centre quaternion).

fields.name: cone
fields.doc: Differentiate the minimal rotation aligning tool Z to a fixed cone axis.

types.name: OrientationLattice
types.doc: Native orientation cells, shared by geometric candidate families.

fields.name: centre
fields.doc: Align the cone axis while preserving the target's spin preference.

types.name: PathDifferential
types.doc:
Differential q'(s), q''(s) at an analytically solved configuration.
J comes from compiled kinematics. J' is its centred directional difference
along q'; joint derivatives themselves are solved from the task relation.

fields.name: solve
fields.signature: (group:KinematicGroup, q:Array<Float>, velocity:Array<Float>, acceleration:Array<Float>, known:Array<Bool>, knownFirst:Array<Float>, knownSecond:Array<Float>, ?differenceStep:Float, ?freeToolAxis:Bool):JointDerivatives

types.name: PathMergeBudget
types.doc: Spend only the Cartesian path allowance not already used by geometry and native lowering.

fields.name: budget
fields.doc: One immutable section's proof, including a proved absence of remaining budget.

types.name: PathPlanner
types.doc: Cartesian planner with immutable machine configuration and no request state.

types.name: PathSample
types.doc: A joint-space sample of a path: where, on which primitive, and the primitive arriving there.

types.name: PathSampler
types.doc: Geometry-only sampling before inverse kinematics and timing. No compiler or solver state is retained.

fields.name: MAX_SECTION_SAMPLES
fields.doc:
Most samples one timed section holds. An arm's samples each cost an inverse-kinematics search, so its budget is
small; on a machine whose joints are an exact affine map a straight piece is one sample, and what a section costs is
native memory (a sample is 2 KB).

fields.name: requireBudget
fields.doc: Check the number of spans, excluding the initial sample, against the solver's sampling budget.

fields.name: timingSections
fields.doc:
`path` split at its sharp corners, where one primitive's end tangent is not the next one's start tangent (authored
task-velocity discontinuities, each timed from rest to rest), with each section's distance along it.

fields.name: samples
fields.doc:
Where to sample a path in joint space: every primitive boundary, so that
each span lies on one primitive, and inside each primitive at most
`cartesianResolution` apart and a quarter radian of turning apart. A
boundary sample also names the primitive arriving at it.

types.name: PlanCertification
types.doc: Certifies transformed motion and owns any execution plan until all checks succeed.

fields.name: certify
fields.doc: Borrows pending/transformed trajectories; returns the caller-owned certified plan.

types.name: PlanCertificationContext
types.doc: Typed settings borrowed for synchronous certification; the stage owns none of these inputs.

types.name: PlanCheck
types.doc:
Checks polynomial motion against the drives of the machine it is for:
the torque each motor would need along the plan against what its drive can give (a stepper's
pull-out curve, a servo's peak and rated torque), and how far the axes' drives stretch or lag
under the plan's forces. It reads the plan's polynomial segments, so the same check serves a
simulation and a device.

Rack drives use the same load Jacobian as screws and belts; assembled mesh, reducer and hinge
allowances reach the accuracy check through the coupling compliance and backlash.
The model's actuators, couplings, masses and inertias supply everything: see `DriveLoads`. Joint
`jointIds[i]` is plan joint `i`; axes the plan does not move are not checked.

types.name: PlanCheckOptions
types.doc:
What a plan check assumes about the machine and how much it asks of the drives. The friction
and force defaults are assumptions, not datasheet values: a hobby-class CNC's linear rails drag
a few newtons, and a cutting force depends on the tool, the material and the feed, so a machine
that wants either states it.

types.name: PlanCheckSummary
types.doc: What the plan checks of a run found, added up: the findings and how near the drives came to their limits.

fields.name: MAX_KEPT
fields.doc: Findings kept, most recent last; later ones are only counted.

fields.name: flagged
fields.doc: Plans with at least one finding.

fields.name: speedLimits
fields.doc: Hardware ceilings that explain the compiled planning speeds.

fields.name: count
fields.doc: Findings of one kind.

types.name: PlanExecutor
types.doc: Submits a validated plan in bounded chunks and tracks its owner-clock progress.

fields.name: update
fields.doc: False while a hold or resume command still needs an owner tick before another plan can start.

fields.name: allSubmitted
fields.doc: All current coefficients are queued, so a certified successor may be queued.

types.name: PlanValidator
types.doc: An admission check on the actual timed plan, before any segment is sent.

fields.name: fork
fields.doc: A worker copy, or the same object when the check is immutable.

types.name: PlanningLimits
types.doc: One snapshot of drive-derived planning limits, in the planner's joint order.

fields.name: assumptions
fields.doc: Defaults used where the model does not supply a quantity; never hardware ratings.

fields.name: ofGroup
fields.doc: The same helper over a group's driving joints, preserving its solver order.

fields.name: check
fields.doc: Check the original drive model with the same steady loads used to derive its caps.

types.name: PlanningResult
types.doc: Output of a planning request; diagnostics belong to that request only.

types.name: PosePathRefinement
types.doc:
Task data from authored primitives, retaining both sides of path knots.
The path must already be expressed in the group's task reference frame.

types.name: PreparedProgramPath
types.doc: A planned motion waiting for the ops that may still add to it (internal to compilation).

types.name: PressureAdvanceLimits
types.doc:
Conservative planning bounds for the box average and endpoint taper used by `Trajectory.advanceJoint`.
The executed quintic approximation must still pass continuous trajectory validation.

types.name: ProgramBarrier
types.doc: Host-side condition between independently executable plan blocks.

types.name: ProgramBlock
types.doc:
Exact-stop plans followed by an optional host-side barrier. A block being
planned is open: plans are added as they are made, and it is complete once
its barrier (or the program's end) is reached.

fields.name: open
fields.doc: An open block, to be filled by `add` and finished by `close`.

fields.name: retireFirstPlan
fields.doc: Retire consumed native coefficients and their aligned path/event metadata.

types.name: ProgramBlocks
types.doc:
A program's plans gathered into blocks as they are planned. The last block
stays open until its barrier or the program's end. Owns its plans.

fields.name: done
fields.doc: Whether the whole program is planned.

fields.name: nextPlanId
fields.doc: The next unused plan id, once `done`.

fields.name: hasWork
fields.doc: Whether there is a plan or barrier to execute yet.

fields.name: finishedBlocks
fields.doc: The blocks of a finished program, without the empty block its end may close.

types.name: ProgramCompilation
types.doc:
A program being planned one op at a time, so execution can start on the
first plans while later ones are still to be made. Each step delivers what
it plans to `sink`, which owns the plans from then on; a compilation owns
only the motion it has not finished planning.

fields.name: done
fields.doc: Whether every op is planned.

fields.name: speedScale
fields.doc: The speed of paths planned from now on, as a fraction of their programmed speed.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (compiler:ProgramCompiler, program:MotionProgram, initialQ:Array<Float>, firstPlanId:Int64, firstOp:Int, speedScale:Float, sink:ProgramSink):Void

fields.name: step
fields.doc: Plans the next op, or the next stretch of a path op. Returns false once the whole program is planned.

fields.name: nextPlanId
fields.doc: The id the next plan will take.

fields.name: dispose
fields.doc: Disposes the motion not yet delivered; delivered plans belong to the sink.

types.name: ProgramCompiler
types.doc: Lowers an authored program to validated, exact-stop plans.

fields.name: planningAssumptions
fields.doc: Planning defaults exposed to callers alongside the drive check's physical assumptions.

fields.name: maxJointJump
fields.doc: The speed scale of the program being compiled.

fields.name: planCheck
fields.doc:
The plan check every compiled program goes through, or null for none, for simulation and device.
Its findings are on `ExecutionPlan.checked`. Direct MotionSystem moves and live ServoSession
plan chunks run their checks at their submission boundaries.

fields.name: motorSpace
fields.doc: Linear motor sums for machines whose axis velocities use the single-axis envelope.

fields.name: mergeSegmentsSeconds
fields.doc:
When positive, runs of a lowered path's segments are merged into one quintic each, up to this long, where the
quintic stays inside the path's remaining approximation budget. A printer's curves lower to thousands of segments a second, which would
fill the robot's queue and a device's link; the default of zero leaves a path as it was lowered.

fields.name: maximumPathPlanSeconds
fields.doc: Maximum continuous path publication duration, supplied by the owning planner. Null leaves it unbounded.

fields.name: mergeBudgetForMotion
fields.doc: Optional pure, worker-safe budget factory for other kinematics; affine XYZ paths derive theirs from geometry.

fields.name: mergeBudgetRefusals
fields.doc: Requested merges retained as authored because no positive geometric remainder could be proved.

fields.name: mergeRefusals
fields.doc:
How many plans were built from the lowered path because their merged form broke a limit, and why the last one did. A
plan that was not merged (merging off, a joint move) is not a refusal.

fields.name: pressureAdvance
fields.doc: Seconds a path's distance-driven joint (an extruder) runs ahead of the flow it feeds; 0 is off.

fields.name: pressureAdvanceWindow
fields.doc: The window, seconds, over which the driven joint's velocity is averaged for the advance.

fields.name: pathEventSchedule
fields.signature: :Null<(Int, Float, Bool, Array<Float>, Array<Float>, Array<PathEvent>) -> Array<PathEvent>>
fields.doc:
Pure, worker-safe event scheduling on the actual timed path section.
Distances/events use whole-operation coordinates; times are section-local.

fields.name: requireFeasiblePath
fields.doc: Process sections reject a time-law retry or stretch after refinement.

fields.name: clearanceEvents
fields.doc:
Changes to the cell during the program, per op (grasps, places, contact windows; COLLISION.md
CL-D9). Validation replays them in time order through the planner's clearance world, which must
then be a `ClearanceScene`.

fields.name: clearanceDepthLimit
fields.doc: How deep the conservative clearance check of a joint or generated move bisects (CL4b).

fields.name: angularResolution
fields.doc: Maximum task rotation per selection sample, in radians; clearance is certified separately.

fields.name: motionPlanner
fields.doc: Plans the path of a joint move whose options ask for it (`MotionOptions.planned`; COLLISION.md CL7).

fields.name: flyByCertificate
fields.doc:
Certifies the curved motion of planned joint moves joined by `Blend.FlyBy`; it must be the
space `motionPlanner` checks its edges in. Without it a fly-by stops at its target.

fields.name: MAX_SECTION_SAMPLES
fields.doc: Sampling budgets retained here for callers of the compiler's existing API.

fields.name: shapeJoints
fields.doc:
Shapes the motion of the joints that have a shaper (`shapers`, one entry per joint in joint order, null for a joint
that is not shaped): each path's motion is convolved with the shaper's impulses, which keeps the carriage from
ringing at the machine's resonance. A joint without a shaper (the other axis, the extruder) is delayed by the same
average, so everything stays in step, and the path's events with it. Joints that follow others are shaped through
their leaders. Shaping is only meaningful where a joint's motion is the tool's (Cartesian axes): the task-space
check allows the shaped tool the spread that the impulses can open between the motion and its delayed copy.

fields.name: withJointPathPlanner
fields.doc: Preserve compiler limits/checks while timing an already selected route.

fields.name: forWorker
fields.doc:
This compiler for a planning thread, on a fork of its solver: the worker never shares solver
state with the caller, who keeps using the same kinematics while plans execute.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (solver:KinematicsSolver, limits:ValidationLimits, frameId:String, maxVelocity:Array<Float>, maxAcceleration:Array<Float>, maxJerk:Array<Float>, startTolerances:StartTolerances, ?timing:PathTimingBackend, ?cartesianResolution:Float, ?maxJointJump:Float, ?positionTolerance:Float, ?orientationTolerance:Float, ?ikTolerance:IkTolerance, ?jointPathPlanner:JointPathPlanner, ?perJointMaxJump:Array<Float>, ?jointIds:Array<String>, ?couplings:Array<JointCoupling>, ?controllerPeriodSeconds:Float):Void

fields.name: compile
fields.doc:
Plans `program` from `initialQ`. With `firstOp`, ops before it are taken
as done and the rest is planned, keeping their op indices; `speedScale`
scales every path's speed, within the joint limits as always.

fields.name: begin
fields.doc: Starts planning `program` one op at a time into `sink`; see `ProgramCompilation`.

fields.name: generateEntry
fields.doc:
The stopped joint transition used for free path entry/exit checks.
Caller owns and must dispose the returned trajectory.

fields.name: timingSections
fields.doc: Split a path at authored task-velocity discontinuities, preserving section distances.

types.name: ProgramPlanner
types.doc:
Plans a program on a worker thread, `lookaheadSeconds` of motion ahead of the
plans that have started executing, and hands each step to the frame thread,
which `poll`s them into `blocks`. A single-threaded Wasm host advances the same
compilation cooperatively on demand, retaining bounded lookahead. The worker owns the compilation; the frame
thread owns `blocks` and every plan in it, so neither touches the other's
objects. A speed scale set while planning applies to motion not yet planned.

A worker is inside MotionKit's native library while it plans, and `dispose` returns at once without waiting for it:
the worker finishes the plan it is on and stops. A process that exits while workers are still planning runs the
native library's static destructors under them, which crashes the worker (a use after destruction of the
library's handle tables, seen as a segmentation fault or double free when a program exited just after a weld
that gave up mid-plan). Whoever ends the process, or tears a world down, calls `shutdown` first.

fields.name: blocks
fields.doc: What is planned so far; frame thread only.

fields.name: failure
fields.doc: Why planning stopped, if it failed.

fields.name: nextPlanId
fields.doc: The next unused plan id: one past the last plan delivered.

fields.name: planningMetrics
fields.doc: Worker CPU-phase wall time, excluding lookahead waits, and numeric pose queries.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (compiler:ProgramCompiler, program:MotionProgram, initialQ:Array<Float>, firstPlanId:Int64, firstOp:Int, speedScale:Float, lookaheadSeconds:Float, ?compiled:CompiledProgram):Void
fields.doc: Starts planning; an invalid program or start position throws here, on the caller's thread.

fields.name: fromCompiled
fields.doc: Adopt checked plans without another compilation or a worker thread.

fields.name: active
fields.doc: How many planners have a worker that has not stopped yet.

fields.name: shutdown
fields.doc:
Cancels every planner and waits for its worker to stop, up to `timeoutSeconds` in all, so that no worker is inside
the native library when the process exits or the world is torn down. Returns how many workers were still running
when the time ran out (none, normally).

fields.name: poll
fields.doc: Moves what the worker has planned since the last poll into `blocks`; true if anything came.

fields.name: waitForMore
fields.doc: Waits until the worker delivers more or stops, then polls.

fields.name: isStopped
fields.doc: Whether the worker has stopped: the program is planned, planning failed, or it was cancelled.

fields.name: started
fields.doc: Execution has started `count` plans in all; the worker stays `lookaheadSeconds` past them.

fields.name: dispose
fields.doc: Stops the worker and disposes every plan, delivered or not. Returns at once.

types.name: ProgramSink
types.doc: Receives what a ProgramCompilation plans, in program order.

fields.name: plan
fields.doc: A finished plan of op `opIndex`; the sink owns it from here.

fields.name: barrier
fields.doc: The current block ends at `barrier`; later plans start the next block.

fields.name: note
fields.doc: A nonfatal planning note.

fields.name: finish
fields.doc: The whole program is planned, its last block ends, and `nextPlanId` is the next unused plan id.

types.name: QueuedMotionRequest
types.doc: Queued command payloads held behind a replacement stop.

types.name: RedundancyCurve
types.doc: Smooth redundancy geometry shared by refinement and differentiation.

types.name: RedundancyParameterization
types.doc:
Names the motion a group has left once its tool pose is fixed
(KINEMATICS.md KK-D19), so `RedundancyResolver` can choose it along a
whole path: the swivel of a 7-axis arm, the values of a cell's external
axes, later a mobile base's pose.

fields.name: preferringOrientation
fields.doc: Sets the soft orientation preference; preferTarget uses each target when preference is null.

fields.name: preferringPosture
fields.doc: Sets the arm posture preference, leaving external axes free to supply the remaining motion.

fields.name: dimension
fields.doc: How many values name the redundancy.

fields.name: valuesAt
fields.doc: The values at `q`, or null where they are undefined (e.g. a straight elbow).

fields.name: solveAt
fields.doc: IK for the tool target with the redundancy held at `values`, seeded by `seed`; null if it does not solve.

fields.name: solveNear
fields.doc: IK keeping the redundancy as near the seed's as the target allows (where `solveAt` is blocked, e.g. by a limit).

fields.name: valuesJacobian
fields.doc:
The values' Jacobian at `q`: `dimension()` rows of one entry per group DOF, row-major
(d values = G · dq), or null where the values are undefined.

fields.name: ratesPerMetre
fields.doc: How far each value may move per metre of path between samples: the resolver's lattice resolution.

fields.name: periodic
fields.doc: True for a value that wraps (an angle), so smoothing never averages across the ±π seam.

fields.name: costFactors
fields.doc: Factor on each group DOF's motion cost in the path search (below 1 makes a DOF the cheaper one to move).

types.name: RedundancyPoses
types.doc: Conversions shared by the redundancy parameterizations.

types.name: RedundancyResolver
types.doc:
Chooses a group's redundancy along a whole path (KINEMATICS.md KK-D19),
for any `RedundancyParameterization`:

1. A beam search over a redundancy lattice. Each of a sample's candidates
continues to the next sample with its redundancy held, and moved one
lattice step up or down in each value (the step is the
parameterization's rate times the distance between the samples); where
a limit blocks the held value, it continues with the redundancy as a
preference. Every new configuration gets its cheapest cost from the
start over all the previous candidates it can follow (no joint moving
more than `maxJump`; each DOF's motion weighed by its cost factor over
its speed), and the `maxCandidates` cheapest, one per lattice cell,
go on. Cheap routes survive whichever way they move; the route is read
back through each candidate's best predecessor.
2. Smooth the route's redundancy (a Gaussian over about an eighth of the
samples, the first pinned, the values reflected through each end so a
steady trend stays straight there) and re-solve every sample exactly there, so
the joints do not step between lattice cells. If a sample does not
solve or a joint would jump, the route stands as found.

fields.name: solvePath
fields.doc: The path for `request`. Throws, naming the sample, where no candidate continues.

fields.name: solve
fields.doc: The path for `request` and, when the route was smoothed, the exact rate of its redundancy along it.

types.name: RedundancySpline
types.doc:
Natural C2 cubic spline in path distance. Periodic values are unwrapped
before fitting; outputs remain unwrapped so their derivatives stay continuous.
Bounds are checked by the downstream analytic refinement, since cubic
interpolation can overshoot its knots.

types.name: RefinedCollision
types.doc: A refined sample failure or the sweep arriving at that sample.

types.name: RefinementTarget
types.doc: Centre rates are six-dimensional spatial derivatives: linear then angular.

types.name: RevoluteReachBound
types.doc:
A necessary reach condition, independent of joint limits and IK seeds.
Fixed spans between revolute pivots retain their length at every posture.
Unsupported chains deliberately have no bound.

fields.name: excludes
fields.doc: Reject only outside the sphere enlarged by the task's allowed errors.

types.name: RuntimeHomingDriver
types.doc: Execute seek/backoff/approach as bounded homing plans and native controlled stops.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (robot:Robot, runtime:RobotRuntime, homes:Array<HomingAxis>, motionAxes:Array<MotionAxis>, afterLatch:() -> Void, ?deviceStop:() -> Bool, ?derived:CouplingProjection):Void
fields.doc: afterLatch resets the caller-owned encoder and stepper-slip monitors.

types.name: RuntimeHomingObserver
types.doc:
Reads homing observations from the same immutable snapshot as the robot's joint state.
Position snapshots use runtime logical coordinates, while switch captures use
physical endpoint coordinates. Explicit translations handle those two source
domains separately; velocities remain unchanged.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (robot:Robot, axes:Array<HomingAxis>, translatePosition:(Int, Float) -> Float, translateEdge:(Int, Float) -> Float):Void

types.name: SelectedJointPathPlanner
types.doc:
Reuse globally selected geometry for execution timing. No inverse solving or
fallback selection: a different task, grid or start must be selected again.
The checking planner still validates actual generated/timed trajectories.

types.name: SerialCandidateSampler
types.doc: Combined native serial-arm sampling, including model-derived external transforms.

types.name: SerialCellModel
types.doc: Exports external space screws in the group's root frame, once per model.

types.name: ServoPlan
types.doc:
The plan stream `ServoSession` keeps on robots that execute plans rather
than joint targets (the virtual device), and the host's copy of its end.

Each chunk is one control period appended at the end of the queue: every
arm joint ramps at constant acceleration from its velocity there to the
servo's next velocity (other joints hold still), so chunks join with
continuous position and velocity and a step in acceleration (they are
jerk-unchecked). Chunks do not end at rest while servoing; a braking
stream's last chunk does. Should the host stall, the queue runs dry while
moving, and the runtime or device brakes each joint at its limit.

fields.name: accelerationLimits
fields.doc: A hair under each arm joint's acceleration limit, so ramps cannot exceed it by rounding.

fields.name: streaming
fields.doc: True while the queue holds this stream's chunks.

fields.name: endedAtRest
fields.doc: True once the stream's last chunk ended at rest.

fields.name: endNs
fields.doc: End of the queue on the plan clock, and every joint's state there.

fields.name: begin
fields.doc: Starts a new stream from rest at `positions` (every joint): the robot's setpoint, where a new plan anchors.

fields.name: armPosition
fields.doc: The arm joints' state at the end of the queue, in arm order.

fields.name: chunk
fields.doc:
The next chunk: `durationNs` from the end of the queue, ramping the arm
joints to `velocity` (arm order). The first chunk of a stream starts a
new plan; later ones append to it.

fields.name: accept
fields.doc: Records a chunk the robot accepted: the queue now ends where it does.

fields.name: clear
fields.doc: Forgets the stream: its queue drained (at rest, or run dry and braked by the robot).

types.name: ServoPlanOptions
types.doc: Settings for servoing through streamed plan chunks (see `ServoSession`).

fields.name: leadSeconds
fields.doc:
How much motion to keep queued ahead of execution. It must cover the
gap between updates plus the link (a device commits segments that far
ahead), and it is the servo's latency and how long a stalled host lets
the arm run on before the queue runs dry.

fields.name: accelerationLimits
fields.doc:
The cell's commissioned acceleration limit for each arm joint, as its planners use; null takes each joint's
model limit.

types.name: ServoSession
types.doc:
Live Cartesian servoing of an arm (jogging, teleoperation) as a cyclic
reference (motionkit/plans/LANE_D_REDUNDANCY_SERVO.md, LD-D3), not a queue
of trajectories to replace:

- an operator submits tool twists (base frame, at the TCP) with a sequence
and a deadline on the robot's clock; older sequences, non-finite twists
and already-passed deadlines are rejected;
- every robot tick, `update` reads the snapshot, takes one bounded,
acceleration-limited `ManipulatorServo` step towards the live twist and
submits the resulting joint velocities;
- when the deadline passes without a newer command (or on `stop`), the
twist becomes zero and the arm brakes to rest within its acceleration
limits, so a lost operator leaves the arm standing, not moving on.

The clock is the snapshot's `sourceTimestampNs`. The joint targets carry
the deadline too (braking ones a two-period keepalive), so if the host
stalls, the runtime brakes each joint to zero within its own acceleration
limit. That brake is plain per joint, so the tool leaves its line and a
joint may reach its limit; while `update` runs, the session's brake keeps
the servo's limits. Joint targets are sticky in the runtime, so braking
ends with exact zeros, sent without a deadline.

With `ServoPlanOptions` the session drives robots that execute plans
instead (the virtual device): `update` keeps a short stream of one-period
`ServoPlan` chunks queued ahead of execution, each stepping the servo from
the state at the end of the queue (so the servo acts `leadSeconds` ahead).
Braking ends the stream with a chunk at rest. A stalled host lets the
queue run dry within the lead, and the runtime or device then brakes
every joint at its acceleration limit (reporting an underflow).

types.name: ServoStep
types.doc: One servo tick's answer.

fields.name: velocity
fields.doc: Joint velocities, one per arm DOF, in `q` order.

fields.name: fallback
fields.doc: True when the QP did not solve and the clamped Haxe damped step was used instead.

fields.name: qpStatus
fields.doc: Why the QP stopped (`KinematicsKitNativeConstants.KK_QP_*`), or -1 when it threw.

fields.name: limited
fields.doc: Arm DOF indices whose step sits on a position or velocity bound.

fields.name: avoided
fields.doc: Avoidance pairs that bounded the step, and those whose rows had to be relaxed (COLLISION.md CL5).

types.name: ServoTick
types.doc: What one servo tick did.

fields.name: velocity
fields.doc: The joint velocities commanded for the next period, in arm order.

fields.name: braking
fields.doc: True while no live command is being followed and the arm is braking (or at rest).

fields.name: atRest
fields.doc: True once braking has brought every joint to rest.

types.name: StartTolerances
types.doc: Per-joint runtime start-state tolerances in solver joint order.

types.name: StepperSlip
types.doc:
Carries out what a plan check predicts for steppers: where the motors of an axis would lose sync, the
simulated axis falls behind its command and keeps the error, as a stepper that lost steps does. The
slip is a per-joint offset applied to the commands in the simulation's endpoint, not a change to the
plan, so the runtime and a monitor still see the commanded positions and the machine the real ones.

A plan the check passes has no slip, so it never changes what the machine does. The caller feeds it
each plan's check when the plan starts and the plan's elapsed time as it runs. Joints coupled to a
slipping axis get the offset through their couplings.

fields.name: new
fields.doc:
`jointOfAxis` maps an axis id to its robot joint index; `couplings` are the robot's, to carry the
offset to coupled joints; `sink` sets one joint's offset in the simulation.

fields.name: start
fields.doc: A plan starts: what the check found for it is carried out as it runs.

fields.name: update
fields.doc: The running plan is `elapsed` seconds in.

fields.name: settle
fields.doc: The plan ended, completed or not: what was lost so far is kept.

fields.name: lost
fields.doc: Distance axis `axis` is behind its command, in its units, since the last reset: signed along the motion.

fields.name: slipped
fields.doc: Whether any axis has lost steps.

fields.name: reset
fields.doc: Forgets all lost steps, as homing the machine does, and puts every joint back on its command.

fields.name: rebaseAfterHoming
fields.doc: Clear loss history after calibration without changing any physical endpoint offset.

contactPose is a pure worker-safe policy over TCP poses in the task frame;

types.name: TimedMotion
types.doc: What `TimedMotionTransforms` makes of a timed motion; it owns the trajectories it made (not the motion it was given).

fields.name: executed
fields.doc:
What is executed when the merged form is refused: the shaped motion when there is shaping (shaped from the pre-shape
merge, so already within half the merge tolerances of the advanced one), else the coupled (and advanced) one, else the
lowered one.

fields.name: merged
fields.doc: `executed` merged into longer pieces, or null when merging is off or was refused.

fields.name: shaped
fields.doc: Whether the executed motion is shaped, and so ends the shaper's tail later.

fields.name: dropMerged
fields.doc: The merged path broke a limit: it goes as `executed`.

types.name: TimedMotionBuffer
types.doc:
Worker-owned continuous filter context. Accepting raw timing here never
publishes execution. Retire a preview only after the caller certifies its
transformed motion, joining state and events. No accepted output is retimed.

fields.name: append
fields.doc: Copies raw polynomials; their timing/geometry certificate belongs to the caller.

fields.name: retireCertified
fields.doc: The caller has certified output and owns its execution plan independently.

types.name: TimedMotionChunk
types.doc: Independently owned output and speculative retained context.

types.name: TimedMotionTransforms
types.doc:
The transforms a lowered path's timed motion goes through on its way to a plan: the pressure advance (the driven joint
runs ahead of itself), the coupled joints projected again after each, the input shaper (cut after the advance's own cuts
are merged away, so it works on the plan's segments), and the merge of runs of segments for the link. It returns the
motion that is executed, its merged form, and owns the intermediate trajectories' disposal.

fields.name: apply
fields.doc:
`pending` is the lowered motion; shaping moves its events and times by the shaper's delay. `mark` names the stage just
finished, for the compile profile.

types.name: TimingSectionCursor
types.doc: Lazily constructs only the current exact-stop section and its local drive.

types.name: ToolFreedom
types.doc: The hard tool task shared by pose IK, differential IK and path checks.

fields.name: twistRows
fields.doc: Rows that project a six-component twist onto the hard task at this pose.

fields.name: requiredAngular
fields.doc: Angular path rate that the hard task actually requires, in the path frame.

types.name: TrajectoryClearance
types.doc: Sweep the generated joint curve, retaining CollisionClearance's sampled sweep contract.

types.name: TrajectoryClearanceProof
types.doc:
A conservative clearance check of a timed trajectory (COLLISION.md CL-D5,
CL4b), for joint moves and generated entry, exit and hold moves, whose
timed joint path need not be straight.

Over a time interval of half-length h around t, joint j moves at most
`velocity[j] * h` from q(t), since the validated plan keeps every joint
within its velocity limit; the world's displacement bounds turn those
joint ranges into per-body inflation. The interval is clear when q(t) is
clear with the inflation; otherwise it is bisected, down to `depthLimit`.
At each midpoint the configuration is also checked as it is: a violation
there is a real one, found between the sampled check's samples.

Changes (`ClearanceEvent`) are applied in time order through the world's
`ClearanceScene`, and no interval crosses one.

Contact: with a contact policy over configurations (`contactAt`) the
bound needs the whole interval to be in the contact zone, which only a
neighbourhood policy (`neighbourhood`, given the TCP's displacement bound)
can say; without one the bound uses the stricter margins, and the
midpoint check uses `contactAt`.

fields.name: closed
fields.doc: True when the bound closed every interval.

fields.name: failure
fields.doc: A real violation, found at `failureTime`.

fields.name: openStart
fields.doc: The first interval the bound could not close (bisection at its depth limit).

fields.name: closest
fields.doc: The closest pair at a few times along the motion (informational), and when.

fields.name: run
fields.signature: (world:ClearanceWorld, trajectory:TimedJointTrajectory, velocity:Array<Float>, contact:Bool, ?contactAt:(Array<Float>) -> Bool, ?neighbourhood:(Array<Float>, Float) -> Bool, ?events:Array<ClearanceEvent>, ?depthLimit:Int, ?closestSamples:Int):TrajectoryClearanceProof
fields.doc:
Checks `trajectory` against `world`. `velocity` bounds each joint's speed
over the whole motion; `events` (this motion's, in any order) need a
world that is a `ClearanceScene`; `closestSamples` closest-pair queries
are spread over the motion.

types.name: TrajectoryStream
types.doc: Bounded owner-clock stream shared by machine motion and validated programs.

fields.name: BUFFER_SECONDS
fields.doc: Seconds of motion a stream keeps submitted ahead of the robot.

fields.name: CHUNK_SECONDS
fields.doc:
Seconds of motion one call adds at most. The robot checks every segment it
takes, so topping the buffer up a little a tick keeps that cost even
instead of a burst when a plan starts or the buffer runs low.

fields.name: MIN_LEAD_SECONDS
fields.doc: Seconds of motion always submitted ahead of the robot, however long its ticks.

fields.name: checkMotion
fields.doc: Check the whole direct move once, before any part reaches the robot.

fields.name: observe
fields.doc: Observe and submit through the same fault boundary for axes and arms.

fields.name: fill
fields.signature: (session:MotionSession, build:(Int, Int, Int64, Int64, Int64) -> ExecutionPlanSubmission, describeFailure:(Int, Int, Dynamic) -> String):Void
fields.doc:
Keeps a bounded window of motion submitted ahead of the robot, whatever
the transport and within the room left in its queue: one submission a
call, of `CHUNK_SECONDS` or as much as brings the robot's lead to
`MIN_LEAD_SECONDS`, until `BUFFER_SECONDS` is ahead.

Build a program chunk over the robot's joints from the plan's segment

types.name: CollisionPairRecord
types.doc: The pair and segment a clearance check names; object ids are -1 when unknown.

types.name: ExecutionPlan
types.doc:
Validated, immutable native trajectory with explicit start-state
assumptions. Its segments stay in native memory: the `segment*` spans read
them in place while the plan is alive, and `segments()` copies them out.

fields.name: checked
fields.doc: What a plan check found, set by the compiler that made the plan when it ran one.

fields.name: endsAtRest
fields.doc: False only for a certified publication cut inside continuous motion.

fields.name: COEFFICIENT_STRIDE
fields.doc: Coefficients stored per joint and segment in `segmentCoefficients`: degree zero through five.

fields.name: guarantees
fields.doc: Validation claims carried with this plan's telemetry.

fields.name: segmentStarts
fields.doc: Each segment's start, in nanoseconds from the plan's start.

fields.name: segmentCoefficients
fields.doc:
Joint `j`'s coefficient of power `p` in segment `i` is at
`(i * jointCount + j) * COEFFICIENT_STRIDE + p`, zero above the segment's degree.

fields.name: segments
fields.doc: Copies the segments out of native memory.

fields.name: create
fields.signature: (trajectory:Trajectory, limits:ValidationLimits, planId:Int64, positions:Array<Float>, velocities:Array<Float>, accelerations:Array<Float>, positionTolerances:Array<Float>, velocityTolerances:Array<Float>, accelerationTolerances:Array<Float>, ?events:Array<TimedEvent>):ExecutionPlan
fields.doc: Does not infer derivatives from degree-1 chords; callers supply the authored state.

types.name: InputShaper
types.doc:
An input shaper: a short sequence of impulses that a motion is convolved with so that it excites little vibration in
a mode of the given frequency and damping. The frequency and damping ratio are the machine's data: the resonance of
the belt springs and the mass they carry.

fields.name: frequency
fields.doc: The mode to cancel, hertz.

fields.name: damping
fields.doc: Its damping ratio (0 for an undamped mode, 0.1 is typical of a belt-driven carriage).

fields.name: named
fields.doc: A shaper by the name its kind goes by in a project (`zv`, `mzv`, `ei`).

fields.name: forFrequencyBand
fields.doc: A fixed shaper centered on a physical travel envelope; refuses a band this impulse family cannot suppress.

types.name: InputShaperKind
types.doc: The impulse sequences input shaping offers (Singhose's names, with the formulas Klipper's shapers use).

fields.name: ZV
fields.doc: Zero vibration: two impulses, half a damped period apart. The shortest, the least robust to a wrong frequency.

fields.name: MZV
fields.doc: Modified zero vibration: three impulses over three quarters of a period; leaves under 10 % of the vibration for a frequency 10 % off (ZV about twice that).

fields.name: EI
fields.doc: Extra insensitive: three impulses over a whole period, the longest tail; designed to keep vibration under 5 % across a band around the frequency.

types.name: MotionLimits
types.doc:
Scalar limits used by a trajectory planner.

A zero value means that the caller has not supplied a usable limit yet; a
planner must resolve it from the machine or reject the request. Jerk is
carried from the beginning so planners can add S-curve profiles without
changing the public motion API.

types.name: PathDerivativeEstimate
types.doc: The shared path derivative source for STOP and hold-lead calculations.

types.name: PlanCheckResult
types.doc: What checking one plan found: its diagnostics and how near the limits it came.

fields.name: speedLimits
fields.doc: Active hardware speed ceilings; these explain planning limits rather than flagging violations.

fields.name: worstTorqueRatio
fields.doc: The largest torque a motor needed over what its drive gives at that speed (1 is exactly at the limit); 0 when no motor is checked.

fields.name: worstDeviation
fields.doc: The largest deviation an axis's drive allows, in metres (radians for a turning axis).

fields.name: slips
fields.doc: Where steppers over their curve would lose sync, for a simulation to carry out; empty when none would.

fields.name: locate
fields.doc: Fills each diagnostic's distance along the op's path from the plan's path timeline (times and distances alike).

types.name: PlanDiagnostic
types.doc:
One finding of a plan check: which op of the program, which motor or axis, where in the plan,
and how far over its limit. A check reports its worst sample for each motor and kind, with how
many samples were over.

fields.name: opIndex
fields.doc: The program op the plan came from, -1 when unknown.

fields.name: subject
fields.doc: The actuator that is over its limit, or the axis for an accuracy finding.

fields.name: axis
fields.doc: The axis joint the motor drives, or the axis itself.

fields.name: timeSeconds
fields.doc: Time from the start of the plan at the worst sample, in seconds.

fields.name: pathDistance
fields.doc: Distance along the op's path at the worst sample, when the plan knows its path; -1 otherwise.

fields.name: value
fields.doc: The needed torque (N m) or deviation (m) at the worst sample.

fields.name: limit
fields.doc: What the drive can give there (N m), or the tolerance (m).

fields.name: samples
fields.doc: How many samples of the plan were over.

fields.name: assumed
fields.doc: Assumed model inputs behind this finding.

fields.name: quantities
fields.doc: Quantities used by each finding's calculation.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (kind:PlanDiagnosticKind, opIndex:Int, subject:String, axis:String, timeSeconds:Float, value:Float, limit:Float, samples:Int):Void

fields.name: ratio
fields.doc: How much of its limit the sample asks for: 1.2 is 20% over.

fields.name: describe
fields.doc: Plain-sentence description; `line` is the source line of the op when the caller knows it, else 0.

types.name: PlanDiagnosticKind
types.doc: What a plan check found wrong with a plan, as a name that stays the same in logs and tests.

fields.name: StepperStall
fields.doc: A stepper is asked for more torque than its pull-out curve gives, so it would lose steps.

fields.name: ServoPeakTorque
fields.doc: A servo is asked for more than its peak torque (or more speed than it has torque for).

fields.name: ServoRatedTorque
fields.doc: A servo's torque over a plan, as a root mean square, is above its rated torque.

fields.name: Accuracy
fields.doc: The axis's drive stretches or lags by more than the tolerance.

types.name: PlanLimitError
types.doc: A rejected plan still carries the validation report.

fields.name: toString
fields.doc: Names each failed check with the joint, time, value and limit where it failed.

types.name: PlanSlip
types.doc:
How far an axis falls behind its command in a plan because its stepper motors lost sync: the
distance lost along the axis at the plan times where it was losing (signed along the motion,
constant between those times' ends), and the whole-plan total as full steps of the first motor.

fields.name: motors
fields.doc: The actuators that lost sync together, all of the axis's motors.

fields.name: times
fields.doc: Plan times (s) and the cumulative distance lost then, in the axis's units; both rise together.

fields.name: steps
fields.doc: Full steps of the first motor the plan loses, a positive count.

fields.name: lostAt
fields.doc: The distance lost by plan time `time`: nothing before the first loss, the total after the last.

fields.name: total
fields.doc: The distance the whole plan loses.

types.name: ShaperImpulses
types.doc:
The impulses a joint's motion is convolved with: the shaped motion is the sum of the original motion delayed by each
delay and weighted by its amplitude. The amplitudes are positive and add up to 1, so the shaped motion stays within the
original's velocity and acceleration and only its timing changes: it ends `tail()` later and lags `meanDelay()` on
average.

fields.name: delay
fields.doc: Impulses that only delay by `seconds`: what a joint that is not shaped runs beside shaped ones, to stay in step.

fields.name: tail
fields.doc: Delay of the last impulse: the shaped motion ends this long after the original.

fields.name: meanDelay
fields.doc: The amplitude-weighted mean of the delays: how far the shaped motion lags the original on average.

fields.name: later
fields.doc: The same impulses `seconds` later: the shaping lined up with another joint's.

fields.name: residual
fields.doc:
What is left of a sinusoid of `frequencyHz` and damping ratio `systemDamping` that the motion would excite, as a
fraction of what the unshaped motion excites (Singhose's residual vibration: the magnitude of the impulses' phasors
weighted by their amplitudes and the decay until the last impulse).

fields.name: residualBound
fields.doc:
Upper bound over a continuous frequency band, not just sampled resonances.
Each interval's nearest endpoint is at most half its width away. The sum of the absolute phasor derivatives is a
Lipschitz bound, including decay; refine until its contribution is below accuracy.

types.name: TimedJointTrajectory
types.doc: Read-only timed joint motion. The caller retains ownership of its native storage.

types.name: Trajectory
types.doc: Owns a native piecewise-polynomial joint trajectory.

fields.name: controlAcceleration
fields.doc: Requested joint acceleration for controlled stops; independent of physical ratings.

fields.name: MAX_SHAPER_IMPULSES
fields.doc: The most impulses one joint's shaper may have (`MK_MAX_SHAPER_IMPULSES`).

fields.name: fromSegments
fields.doc: Builds a native trajectory from already-timed polynomial segments.

fields.name: selectJoints
fields.doc: Owned native polynomial copy of the selected joints; preserves the clock origin.

fields.name: sliceTicks
fields.doc: Copy an integer-clock range and rebase its first instant to zero.

fields.name: interiorTimeAtOrBefore
fields.doc: A representable cut inside a polynomial, avoiding its one-sided knot states.

fields.name: concatenate
fields.doc:
Copy polynomial pieces in native code, without converting segments to Haxe objects.
This preserves each piece; the caller still certifies its joining boundaries.

fields.name: fromPositionSamples
fields.doc: Builds a degree-1 trajectory directly from authored positions.

fields.name: generateStateToState
fields.signature: (currentPosition:Array<Float>, currentVelocity:Array<Float>, currentAcceleration:Array<Float>, targetPosition:Array<Float>, maximumVelocity:Array<Float>, maximumAcceleration:Array<Float>, maximumJerk:Array<Float>, ?phase:Bool, ?targetVelocity:Array<Float>):Trajectory
fields.doc:
Offline, jerk-limited synchronized state-to-state motion. With `phase`,
every joint follows one profile scaled to its distance, so a move from
rest to rest is a straight line in joint space (a planned edge).
`targetVelocity` (default rest) lets the motion pass its target moving.

fields.name: segments
fields.doc: Copies polynomial coefficients for submission to an executor.

fields.name: projectCouplings
fields.doc:
A copy whose coupled joints are exactly the sum of their terms (`follower = ratio * leader + offset`, summed
over its terms): `followers`, `leaders`, `ratios` and `offsets` list the terms grouped by follower, each
follower after the joints it follows. Done in native memory: a long trajectory has millions of coefficients.

fields.name: mergeSegments
fields.signature: (positionTolerance:Array<Float>, velocityTolerance:Array<Float>, accelerationTolerance:Array<Float>, velocityLimit:Array<Float>, accelerationLimit:Array<Float>, positionLower:Array<Float>, positionUpper:Array<Float>, maxSeconds:Float):Trajectory
fields.doc:
A copy in which runs of segments are one quintic each where that quintic stays within the per-joint tolerances of
what it replaces (see `mk_merge_segments`): a path lowered to hundreds of short segments a second becomes a few
hundred, which fit a robot's queue and a device's link. Joints that follow others are to be projected again after.

fields.name: mergePositionBudget
fields.doc: Merge within joint-position allowances; derivative error bounds use each candidate's actual duration.

fields.name: shape
fields.doc:
A copy convolved with an input shaper (see `mk_shape_trajectory`): joint `j` is the sum of its original motion
delayed by each of `delays[j]`, weighted by `amplitudes[j]` (positive, adding up to 1). The motion is held at rest
beyond its ends, so the copy is as much longer as the longest delay. Joints that follow others are to be projected
again afterwards.

fields.name: advanceJoint
fields.doc:
A copy in which joint `joint` runs `leadSeconds` ahead of itself, the lead taken on its velocity averaged over
`windowSeconds`: an extruder's pressure advance. The joints that follow it are to be projected again afterwards.

fields.name: advanceJointContext
fields.doc:
Pressure advance with the true continuous-motion origin and end flag.
The caller retains filter context and crops artificial context edges.

fields.name: estimatePathDerivatives
fields.doc: Degree-1 uses chord differences; degree 0 and degree >= 2 use analytic derivatives.

types.name: TrajectoryState
types.doc: Analytic state of a native polynomial trajectory at one instant.

types.name: TrajectoryStateBuffer
types.doc:
One shared native output buffer for trajectory and plan evaluations.

A `mk_trajectory_state` is 2 KB because its arrays are sized for `MK_MAX_JOINTS`, however many joints a
robot has. Allocating and zeroing one per evaluation dominated a simulation tick, so evaluations borrow
this buffer instead: `acquire`, make the native call, `copyOut`, and always `release`. The native call
sets `joint_count` and writes only that many entries, and `copyOut` reads no more than that, so stale
entries beyond it are never observed.

fields.name: acquire
fields.doc: Locks the shared buffer. Every `acquire` needs exactly one `release`, including when the call throws.

fields.name: copyOut
fields.doc: Copies the joint values the last native call wrote. Call between `acquire` and `release`.

fields.signature: (status:Int, joint:Int, derivativeOrder:Int, method:Int, value:Float, timeSeconds:Float, limit:Float, margin:Float, tolerance:Float, resolutionNs:Int64):Void

types.name: ValidationGuarantees
types.doc: Per-check validation claims; sampled checks are not continuous proofs.

fields.name: collision
fields.doc: Clearance against the cell (COLLISION.md CL4b); unchecked without a clearance world.

fields.name: new
fields.signature: (jointPosition:ValidationGuarantee, jointVelocity:ValidationGuarantee, jointAcceleration:ValidationGuarantee, jerk:ValidationGuarantee, continuity:ValidationGuarantee, taskSpace:ValidationGuarantee, collision:ValidationGuarantee):Void

types.name: ValidationLimits
types.doc: Explicit claims about one native trajectory. Each derivative claim carries its presence separately from its value.

fields.name: timeResolutionNs
fields.doc: Executor clock resolution in nanoseconds; zero uses 1 ns. Round fractional device ticks up.

fields.name: withoutJerk
fields.doc: Preserve machine claims while leaving path-timed jerk unclaimed.

fields.name: withStartTolerance
fields.doc:
The same claims for a plan that starts at a state with these position tolerances. A joint resting just outside a
claimed position bound, within its tolerance (a stepper homed onto a limit comes to rest a step or two past it), may
begin there: the validator widens its bound to the start position and no further (`mk_limits_admit_start`).

fields.name: admittedBounds
fields.doc: The position bounds a joint starting at `start` is held to, by the validator's own start-at-limit rule.

types.name: ValidationReport
types.doc: Snapshot of native extrema and their claimed limits.

fields.name: collision
fields.doc: Clearance against the cell (planner-owned; see `setCollision`).

fields.name: collisionPair
fields.doc: The pair and segment the clearance check names.

fields.name: setCollision
fields.signature: (status:Int, method:Int, distance:Float, required:Float, timeSeconds:Float, segmentStart:Float, segmentEnd:Float, resolutionNs:Int64, nameA:String, nameB:String, ?objectA:Int, ?objectB:Int):Void
fields.doc:
Records the planner's clearance check (COLLISION.md CL4b): a continuous
bound (`MK_CHECK_METHOD_BOUND`, zero resolution) or a sampled check, the
distance and required clearance of the named pair, when, and over which
segment. Object ids are -1 when the world names bodies only.

fields.name: setTaskSpace
fields.doc: Records a task-space check sampled by the planner's kinematics layer.

fields.name: setTaskSpaceBound
fields.doc:
A continuous whole-path upper bound, with no sampled peak timestamp.
The compiler must own the geometric/lowering certificate.

fields.name: guarantees
fields.doc: Summarizes each check without treating sampled coverage as a proof.
